pack.title: MET Full Practice Pack — B1, B2, B2+
pack.subtitle: Vocabulary, Grammar, Listening, Speaking, Reading, Writing (3 exercise types per skill per level)

pairs.def: to reach a goal through effort
something bought at a low price

exercises.title: B1 Vocabulary in Context
exercises.template: She ___ a healthy lifestyle by exercising daily.
exercises.explanation: maintains = keeps something at a good level.

exercises.title: B1 Word Meaning
exercises.question: Which word means 'to travel to work regularly'?
exercises.explanation: commute = travel between home and work.

pairs.def: open to more than one meaning

exercises.title: B2 Vocabulary in Context
exercises.template: The results ___ a clear upward trend in usage.
exercises.explanation: imply = suggest indirectly.

exercises.title: B2 Word Meaning
exercises.question: Which is a synonym of 'weaken gradually'?
exercises.explanation: undermine = weaken gradually.

exercises.title: B2+ Vocabulary in Context
exercises.template: The new policy will ___ the risk of data loss.
exercises.explanation: mitigate = make less severe.

exercises.title: B2+ Word Meaning
exercises.question: 'Ubiquitous' means:
exercises.explanation: ubiquitous = present everywhere.

exercises.title: B1 Conditionals
exercises.template: If it rains, we ___ the trip.
exercises.explanation: First conditional: if + present, will + base.

exercises.title: B1 Verb Form
exercises.question: Correct: 'She ___ to Paris three times.'
exercises.explanation: Present perfect: has been.

exercises.title: B2 Third Conditional
exercises.explanation: Third conditional: Had + past participle, would have + past participle.

exercises.title: B2 Reported Speech
exercises.question: Reported: 'I am tired' -> He said he ___ tired.
exercises.explanation: Backshift: am -> was.

exercises.title: B2+ Inversion
exercises.template: Were it not for you, we ___.
exercises.explanation: Inversion after 'were it not for' uses would have + past participle.

exercises.title: B2+ Inversion
exercises.question: Correct: 'Rarely ___ such honesty.'
exercises.explanation: Negative adverb at front triggers inversion: do we hear.

exercises.title: B1 Hotel Check-In
exercises.audioText: Reception: Good morning. Do you have a reservation? Guest: Yes, under Maria Silva. Reception: A single room for two nights. Guest: That is right.
exercises.question: What is the guest's name?
exercises.explanation: The guest says 'under Maria Silva'.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: How about the cafe at five?

exercises.title: B1 Speaking Prompt
exercises.prompt: Describe your daily commute in three sentences.

exercises.title: B2 Work Delay
exercises.audioText: The project was delayed because the supplier missed the deadline. As a result, the team worked overtime to finish on time.
exercises.question: Why was the project delayed?
exercises.explanation: The audio states the supplier missed the deadline.

lines.speaker: Manager
lines.text: Can you send the report today?

lines.speaker: Employee
lines.text: I will send it by four.

exercises.title: B2 Speaking Prompt
exercises.prompt: Explain a time you solved a problem at work or school.

exercises.title: B2+ Policy Update
exercises.audioText: The committee's decision, while controversial, underscores a paradigm shift in policy that few analysts had anticipated.
exercises.question: What does the decision show?
exercises.explanation: The audio says it underscores a paradigm shift.

lines.speaker: Lead
lines.text: Then we must revisit our model.

exercises.title: B2+ Speaking Prompt
exercises.prompt: Present an argument for or against remote work in 90 seconds.

exercises.title: B1 Speaking Prompt
exercises.prompt: Talk about your favorite hobby for one minute.

exercises.title: B1 Opening Phrase
exercises.question: Best opening for a short presentation?
exercises.explanation: A clear greeting is the right opening.

exercises.title: B2 Speaking Prompt
exercises.prompt: Give your opinion on social media using reasons and examples.

exercises.title: B2 Polite Disagreement
exercises.question: Most polite way to disagree?
exercises.explanation: Acknowledging then contrasting is polite.

exercises.title: B2+ Speaking Prompt
exercises.prompt: Defend a position on the use of AI in education.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: How do we mitigate the risk?

exercises.title: B2+ Formal Request
exercises.question: Most formal request phrasing?
exercises.explanation: Conditional polite form is most formal.

exercises.title: B1 Reading Comprehension
exercises.context: Tom enjoys cycling to work. It keeps him fit and saves money on transport. He rides even when it rains.
exercises.question: Why does Tom cycle to work?
exercises.explanation: The text says it keeps him fit and saves money.

exercises.title: B1 Reading Grammar
exercises.explanation: helps = third-person singular present.

exercises.title: B2 Reading Comprehension
exercises.context: Cities are expanding green spaces to improve air quality. Residents report better well-being, though maintenance costs rise.
exercises.question: What is the main benefit mentioned?
exercises.explanation: The text cites air quality and well-being.

exercises.title: B2 Reading Grammar
exercises.explanation: Past passive: was published.

exercises.title: B2+ Reading Comprehension
exercises.context: The proliferation of sensors yields unprecedented data, yet privacy frameworks lag behind the technology that produces it.
exercises.question: What is the concern raised?
exercises.explanation: The text states privacy frameworks lag behind technology.

exercises.title: B2+ Reading Grammar
exercises.template: Had they read it, they ___ the risk.
exercises.explanation: Third conditional with past perfect.

exercises.title: B1 Free Writing
exercises.prompt: Write three sentences about your last holiday.
exercises.rubric: Three complete sentences; past tense; clear topic.

exercises.title: B1 Error Correction
exercises.errorText: He go to school every day.
exercises.correctedText: He goes to school every day.

exercises.title: B2 Free Writing
exercises.prompt: Write a paragraph comparing city and village life.
exercises.rubric: Clear comparison; two sides; examples; B2 grammar.

exercises.title: B2 Error Correction
exercises.errorText: If I will have time, I will call you.
exercises.correctedText: If I have time, I will call you.

exercises.title: B2+ Free Writing
exercises.prompt: Write an essay outline on the impact of technology on education.

exercises.title: B2+ Error Correction
exercises.errorText: Despite the rain, but we went out.
exercises.correctedText: Despite the rain, we went out.
